paper.title: Information Directed Sampling for Linear Partial Monitoring

settings.name_in_paper: Linear partial monitoring, globally observable games
unmapped: learner knows the linear observation operators A_x (m-dimensional observations A_x^T theta + noise); reward <x,theta> is not observed
settings.definition_quote: Let $\xX \subset \RR^d$ be a compact set of actions and $\theta \in \RR^d$ be an unknown parameter. For each action $x\in \xX$, let $A_x \in \RR^{d \times m}$ be a known linear observation operator... receives an $m$-dimensional observation $\a_t = A_{x_t}^\T\theta + \epsilon_t$ ... The reward for the learner is $\ip{x_t,\theta}$ and is not observed.

settings.name_in_paper: Linear partial monitoring, locally observable games
unmapped: learner knows the linear observation operators A_x

settings.name_in_paper: Linear partial monitoring on smooth convex action sets with positive curvature (globally observable)
unmapped: learner knows the linear observation operators A_x
settings.definition_quote: Assume that $\xX$ is closed, convex, has a non-empty interior and that $h_{\xX}$ is twice differentiable. Suppose furthermore that the game is globally observable ... and has strictly positive principle curvature everywhere

settings.name_in_paper: Contextual linear partial monitoring, arbitrary context sequence, each game globally observable (conditional IDS)
unmapped: context-dependent observation operators A_x^z known to the learner
settings.definition_quote: Each context $z \in \zZ$ defines a partial monitoring game with action set $\xX_z$ and the observation operators $\{A_x^z\}$... At time $t$, the learner receives a context $z_t \in \zZ$ and chooses an action $x_t \in \xX_{z_t}$.

settings.name_in_paper: Contextual linear partial monitoring, arbitrary context sequence, each game locally observable (conditional IDS)
unmapped: context-dependent observation operators A_x^z known to the learner
settings.definition_quote: If the contextual game is locally observable in the sense that for any $z \in \zZ$, the game $(\xX_z, \aA_z)$ is locally observable with uniformly bounded alignment constant

settings.name_in_paper: Globally observable contextual games with known context distribution (contextual IDS)
unmapped: action set X_z and observation operators depend on an i.i.d. context drawn from a known distribution nu
contextual global observability: differences in one context may be estimable only in another context
settings.definition_quote: Here we study the case where the context follows a known distribution $\nu \in \sP(\zZ)$ ... $\forall z \in \zZ \text{ and } x,y \in \xX_z \Rightarrow \exists z' \in \zZ \text{ s.t. } x-y \in \laspan(A_x : x \in \xX_{z'})$

settings.name_in_paper: Uniformly locally observable contextual games with known context distribution (contextual IDS)
unmapped: action set X_z and observation operators depend on an i.i.d. context drawn from a known distribution nu
contextual local observability with expected alignment alpha(C,nu) <= alpha_0
settings.definition_quote: In contextual games that are uniformly locally observable in the sense that $\alpha(\cC,\nu)\leq \alpha_0$ for any convex set $\cC\subset \RR^d$

settings.name_in_paper: Partial monitoring in reproducing kernel Hilbert spaces
unmapped: observations are known linear operators A_x of the unknown RKHS function f (e.g. gradients, differences)
settings.definition_quote: The linear observation functions are linear operators $A_x : \hH \rightarrow \RR^m$. As before, the observations when choosing $x_t$ are $\a_t = A_{x_t}f + \epsilon_t$.

settings.name_in_paper: Finite linear partial monitoring games (lower bound)
unmapped: learner knows the observation operators A_x
settings.definition_quote: For the remainder of this section, we fix an arbitrary policy and finite game with actions $\xX$ and feedback functions $(A_x)_{x \in \xX}$. For simplicity, we assume the noise is Gaussian and $\xX$ spans $\RR^d$.

settings.name_in_paper: Finite globally (not locally) observable games (lower bound)
unmapped: learner knows the observation operators A_x
settings.definition_quote: Suppose the game is globally observable, but not locally observable.

unmapped: learner knows the observation operators A_x
settings.definition_quote: Suppose the game is locally observable, then there exists a constant $c > 0$ such that for all $n$ there is a $\theta$ for which $R_n(\theta) \geq cn^{1/2}$.

algorithms.name: Information Directed Sampling (IDS) for linear partial monitoring
IDS with directed information gain I_t(x;w_t)

symbols.alpha_w: worst-case alignment constant of the game
symbols.gamma_n: total information gain, <= d log(1 + n m / d)

conditions: rho-subgaussian noise (confidence set as stated uses no rho)

source.label: thm:global-upper
source.quote: For any game that satisfies the global observability condition \eqref{eq:global}, there exists a universal constant $C > 0$ such that for any $n\geq 1$ with probability at least $1 - \delta$, $R_n \leq C n^{2/3} \left(\alpha \beta_n (\gamma_n + \log\tfrac{1}{\delta})\right)^{1/3} + 4\log\left(\frac{4n+4}{\delta}\right)$.

results.notes: Regret is realized sum of <x*-x_t,theta> bounded w.h.p. Gives Õ(n^{2/3}) for fixed d.

symbols.sum_alpha_beta: sum_{t=1}^n alpha(P_t) beta_t, with alpha(P_t) the alignment constant of the plausible maximizer set

source.label: thm:local-upper
source.quote: For locally observable games denote $\alpha_t = \alpha(\pP_t)$. There exists a universal constant $C > 0$ such that for any $n \geq 1$ with probability at least $1-\delta$, $R_n \leq C \sqrt{\sum_{t=1}^n\alpha_t \beta_t \left( \gamma_n + \log \tfrac{1}{\delta} \right)} + 4\log\left(\frac{4n+4}{\delta}\right)$.

results.notes: Data-dependent bound through alpha_t; marked instance_dependent loosely.

symbols.alpha_0: uniform bound on alignment constant alpha(P(C)) over convex C

conditions: uniformly locally observable game: alpha(P(C)) <= alpha_0 for all convex C

source.label: thm:local-upper
source.quote: For games that are uniformly locally observable, the regret bound is $R_n \leq \tilde \oO(\sqrt{\alpha_0 \beta_n \gamma_n n})$.

results.notes: Bandit games have alpha_0 <= 4; linear bandits give Õ(d sqrt(n)).

symbols.C_game: constant depending only on (A_z : z in X)
symbols.kappa_circ: inverse of max eigenvalue of Hessian of support function on unit sphere (curvature)

conditions: X closed, convex, non-empty interior, support function twice differentiable

source.label: thm:convex
source.quote: Assume that $\xX$ is closed, convex, has a non-empty interior and that $h_{\xX}$ is twice differentiable. Suppose furthermore that the game is globally observable ... Then, with probability at least $1 - \delta$, for any $n \geq 1$, $R_n \leq C\sqrt{\max\left(1, \frac{1}{\kappa_{\circ}}\right) \beta_n \left(\gamma_n + \log\tfrac{1}{\delta}\right)n} + 4 \log\left(\frac{4n + 4}{\delta}\right)$

symbols.alpha_w: uniform bound on alignment constant alpha(z) over contexts

conditions: every context game globally observable with alpha(z) <= alpha

source.label: cor:conditional-ids
source.quote: If a contextual game is globally observable in the sense that for any context $z$, the game $(\xX_z, \aA_z)$ is globally observable with uniformly bounded alignment constant $\alpha(z) \leq \alpha$, then for any $n \geq 1$ with probability at least $1-\delta$, conditional IDS achieves $R_n \leq C n^{2/3} ...$

symbols.alpha_0: uniform bound on local alignment alpha(C;z)

conditions: each context game locally observable with alpha(C;z) <= alpha_0 for all convex C

source.label: cor:conditional-ids
source.quote: If the contextual game is locally observable in the sense that for any $z \in \zZ$, the game $(\xX_z, \aA_z)$ is locally observable with uniformly bounded alignment constant $\alpha(\cC;z) \leq \alpha_0$ ... conditional IDS achieves $R_n \leq C \sqrt{n \alpha_0 \beta_n \left( \gamma_n + \log \tfrac{1}{\delta} \right)} + 4\log\left(\frac{4n+4}{\delta}\right)$

source.label: thm:regret-contextual
source.quote: For globally observable contextual games with bounded expected worst-case alignment $\alpha(\nu)$, for any $n \geq 1$, the regret is bounded with probability at least $1-\delta$, $R_n \leq C n^{2/3} \left(\alpha(\nu)\beta_n (\gamma_n + \log \tfrac{1}{\delta})\right)^{1/3} + 4\log\left(\frac{4n+4}{\delta}\right)$.

results.notes: C not explicitly declared universal in statement.

symbols.alpha_0: uniform bound on expected alignment alpha(C,nu)

conditions: alpha(C,nu) <= alpha_0 for every convex C

source.label: thm:regret-contextual-local
source.quote: In contextual games that are uniformly locally observable in the sense that $\alpha(\cC,\nu)\leq \alpha_0$ for any convex set $\cC\subset \RR^d$, the regret is bounded for any $n \geq 1$ with probability at least $1-\delta$, $R_n \leq C \sqrt{\alpha_0 \beta_n n (\gamma_n + \log \tfrac{1}{\delta})} + 4\log\left(\frac{4n+4}{\delta}\right)$.

IDS, defined with the directed information gain $I_t(x;w_t)$, achieves for any $n \geq 1$, with probability at least $1-\delta$, $R_n \leq \oO\big(n^{2/3} (\alpha \beta_n (\gamma_n + \log \tfrac{1}{\delta}))^{1/3}\big)$ on globally observable games
and $R_n \leq \oO\left((\alpha_0 \beta_n (\gamma_n + \log \frac{1}{\delta})n)^{1/2}\right)$ on uniformly locally observable games.

symbols.gamma_n: total information gain log det(K_n + I)

source.quote: The kernelized variant of IDS achieves $R_n \leq \oO\big(n^{2/3} (\alpha \beta_n (\gamma_n + \log \tfrac{1}{\delta}))^{1/3}\big)$ on globally observable games ... for any $n \geq 1$ with probability at least $1-\delta$.
and $R_n \leq \oO\left((\alpha_0 \beta_n (\gamma_n + \log\frac{1}{\delta}) n)^{1/2}\right)$ on uniformly locally observable games for any $n \geq 1$ with probability at least $1-\delta$.

conditions: span(A_x : x in X) != R^d (not globally observable)
finite game, Gaussian noise, X spans R^d

source.label: thm:linear
source.quote: Suppose that $\laspan(A_x : x \in \xX) \neq \RR^d$, then there exists a game-dependent constant $c > 0$ such that for all $n \geq 1$ there exists a $\theta$ for which $R_n(\theta) \geq cn$.

conditions: globally observable but not locally observable finite game

source.quote: Suppose the game is globally observable, but not locally observable. Then there exists a game-dependent constant $c > 0$ and  $\theta \in \RR^d$ such that the regret is $R_n(\theta) \geq c n^{2/3}$.

conditions: constant c depends on the game

source.quote: Suppose the game is locally observable, then there exists a constant $c > 0$ such that for all $n$ there is a $\theta$ for which $R_n(\theta) \geq cn^{1/2}$.

results.notes: Main text states this for games with more than one Pareto optimal action.

conditions: finite locally observable game with more than one Pareto optimal action
minimax expected regret R_n^* = inf_pi sup_theta E[R_n]
results.notes: Classification: Theta up to log factors (paper writes tilde Theta; notation Theta used as closest). Zero-regret case for single Pareto optimal action not recorded separately.
